cover.title: My account
p3s1i0: This screen lets you view and manage your own account. Open it from View profile in the profile menu at the top right. All account-related settings branch out from this screen, which is divided into four areas.
p3s2i0: Concurrent session block notice — A record that your session was ended by a login from another device 1.2. If there is no such record, it is not shown.
p3s2i1: Basic information — Your name and email. Only your name can be changed 1.3.
p3s2i2: My activity management — Five entry points that lead to Password · E-signature password · Pending signatures · Notification settings · Session history 1.4.
p3s2i3: Recent login history — Recent access records for your account 1.5.
p3s3i0: This screen is for your own account only. You cannot view or change other users' information. That function is on the User management screen of the system administrator.
p4.title: Concurrent session block notice
p4s1i0: Only one simultaneous session is allowed per account. If you log in with the same account on another device or browser, the session that was already open ends, and the record is added to this banner. If you did not make this login yourself, your account may have been used without your permission, so you must check it immediately.
p4.cap.1: Records of your session being ended by a login on another device — only the 5 most recent are shown
p4s2i0: View full history — Check all records, including the ones that are omitted 3.3.
p4s2i1: Close — Closing the banner marks all displayed records as checked. This cannot be undone, so close the banner only after you have reviewed its contents.
p4s2i2: The banner shows only the 5 most recent records, and the number of remaining records is indicated below as a number. Each line shows the time of occurrence and the information about the device used to log in.
p4s3i0: If there is an access record you do not remember, change your password immediately and notify your system administrator 2.1.
p5.title: Basic information
p5s1i0: Your name and email are displayed. You can change your name directly, but you cannot change your email, because it is your login account.
p5s2i0: Edit icon — Switches to a state in which you can change your name.
p5s2i1: The name field becomes active. Enter a new name.
p5s2i3: The email field has a gray background and cannot be selected. Below it, the message “Email cannot be changed.” is shown.
p5s2i4: Cancel — Discards your changes and returns to view mode.
p5s3i0: If you need to change your email address, ask your system administrator. Your email is both your login account and the address that receives notifications.
p6.title: My activity management
p6s1i0: Entry points to account-related settings are gathered in one place. Select the button on each card to go to that screen.
p6.cap.1: Five entry points to account-related settings
p6s2i0: Password · Change — Changes your login password 2.1.
p6s2i1: E-signature password · Change — Changes the password used for signing 2.2. It is a separate value from your login password.
p6s2i2: My pending signatures · Go to — Checks the items you need to sign 3.2.
p6s2i3: Notification settings · Configure — Manages whether you receive in-app and email notifications 3.1.
p6s2i4: Session replacement history · View — Checks the full record of sessions ended by a login from another device 3.3.
p6s2i5: The password card also shows the time remaining until the password expires. When expiry is near, a separate indicator appears.
p6s3i0: Passwords expire every 90 days. When a password expires, you are taken to the change screen at your next login, and you cannot proceed with your work until you change it. If the remaining time is shown, change your password in advance.
p7.title: Recent login history
p7s1i0: Access records for your account are shown in order, most recent first. Attempts are recorded even when they did not succeed, so check periodically for any record you do not remember.
p7.cap.1: Recent access records for your account
p7s2i0: The number of records is shown next to the title.
p7s2i1: Each row starts with the access date and time and the result.
p7s2i2: On the right, the device information for the access is shown — in the order of address, browser and operating system.
p7s3i0: This list is the record of access. The banner in 1.2 is the record of your session being cut off by such an access. They are different lists, so check both together.
p8.title: Change password
ch2.title: Password management
sec2.1.title: Change password
sec2.2.title: Change e-signature password
p8s1i0: Changes your login password. Use this screen when you know your current password. If you have forgotten your password, use the reset option on the login screen.
p8.cap.1: Right after opening — no conditions are met yet, so the button is disabled
p8s2i0: Current password — Enter the password you are using now.
p8s2i1: New password — Enter the password you want to use.
p8s2i2: The condition list updates as you type. Each condition you meet changes to a check mark.
p8s2i3: Confirm password — Enter the same value once more.
p8s2i4: Change — Stays disabled until all three fields are correct.
p8s2i5: Password visibility toggle — Shows the entered value in plain text. It is available in all three fields.
p8s2i6: Cancel — Stops the change and returns you to the previous screen.
p8s3i0: The specific conditions and how many there are may vary depending on system settings. Use the list shown on the screen as your reference.
p9.title: Change e-signature password
p9s1i0: Changes the password used for e-signatures. It is a separate value from your login password. When you sign, you are authenticated once more with your user account and this password. Only you can set it, and no separate permission is required.
p9s2i0: Current e-signature password — Enter the e-signature password you are using now.
p9s2i1: New e-signature password — Enter the value you want to use. The complexity rules are the same as for the login password.
p9s2i2: Confirm password — Enter the same value once more.
p9s2i3: The complexity check list updates as you type.
p9s2i4: Save — Stays disabled until all items are met.
p9s2i5: The notice at the top explains what this password is for — it must be different from your login password, and it is used for two-factor authentication when you sign.
p9s2i6: The last item in the list (must differ from the login password) is checked by the system when you save. Whether it is met is not updated while you type.
p9s3i0: E-signing is an activity regulated under 21 CFR Part 11. Do not share your signature password with anyone else. A signature is recorded as performed by you and cannot be canceled.
p10.title: Notification settings
p10s1i0: Manage which notifications you receive, by type. You can turn in-app notifications and email notifications on and off separately.
p10.cap.1: Notification settings (SCR-PLT-003) — whether in-app and email notifications are received for each trigger
p10s2i0: Enable notifications — The master switch. If you turn it off, all notifications are blocked regardless of the settings below.
p10s2i1: In-app — Notifications you receive inside the system screen.
p10s2i2: Email — Notifications you receive at your registered email address.
p10s2i3: Save — Applies the settings you changed. If you have not changed anything, it is disabled.
p10s2i4: The count shown in the title is the number of types you can receive with your permissions, shown together with the total number of types. Notifications you have no permission for do not appear in the list.
p10s2i5: The gray text in each row is a code that identifies the notification type. Giving this code when you contact support speeds up the check.
p10s3i0: If you turn off Enable notifications, important notifications such as account lock or invalid signature are also blocked. We recommend turning off notifications by type instead.
p11.title: Pending signatures
ch3.title: Notifications · Signatures · Sessions
sec3.1.title: Notification settings
sec3.2.title: Pending signatures
sec3.3.title: Session replacement history
p11s1i0: This is the list of items you need to sign. Other people's signing items are not shown, and everyone can check their own list without any separate permission.
p11s2i0: Signing timing — Narrows the list by the point at which a signature is required.
p11s2i3: Search — Searches by signing target or requester.
p11s2i5: The three boxes at the top show the total number of pending items, the number of overdue items, and the number of items on time, respectively.
p11s2i6: The notice box tells you that the signature for the current form is excluded from the requirements, so the signing button is disabled. When the scope is widened, it works again.
p11s2i7: If there are no pending items, an empty list is shown, along with guidance on when items appear.
p11s3i0: Signatures made after the deadline are counted as late signatures and remain in the audit trail. Check the summary boxes at the top first.
p12.title: Session replacement history
p12s1i0: This is the full record of sessions ended by a login from another device. The banner on the profile screen shows only the 5 most recent records, so use this screen to check all of them.
p12.cap.1: Session replacement history (SCR-ACC-009) — full view of the profile banner
p12s2i0: Check status — Shows checked records and unchecked records separately.
p12s2i2: My profile — Returns to the profile screen.
p12s2i3: The table has three columns: time of occurrence · access address · access device.
p12s2i4: The Check column shows a separate mark on each record that has not been checked yet.
p12s3i0: You cannot mark records as checked on this screen. They are marked only when you close the notification banner on the profile screen, and at that time all records shown in the banner are marked as checked together 1.2.
